title: Supported TLS version detection and warnings; lru_cache gotcha
answers: How are supported TLS versions determined?
Why must args to create_proxy_server_context be hashable?
Where are unsupported/insecure TLS version warnings emitted?
body:
- net/tls.py:is_supported_version (@cache) builds a throwaway client SSL.Context with ciphers '@SECLEVEL=0:ALL', sets min=max=version, makes a Connection and recv(): WantReadError -> True, other SSL.Error -> False.
- addons/tlsconfig.py:TlsConfig._warn_unsupported_version iterates Version members using it; warns if the option isn't supported, info if UNBOUNDED and warn_unbound.
- TlsConfig.configure calls it when tls_version_* options change, and _warn_seclevel_missing when min version/ciphers change (warns if min in INSECURE_TLS_MIN_VERSIONS and ciphers lack @SECLEVEL=0).
- Gotcha: create_proxy_server_context and create_client_proxy_context are @lru_cache(256), so all args must be hashable (cipher_list and extra_chain_certs are tuples). Results are cached per arg set.
